family: generic Chromium stealer (browser-named, any valid signer, dropped into Program Files)
evasion_targets: identity::admin_location (identity.rs:511-515) + identity::genuine_browser (identity.rs:~520) — any valid signer + Program Files location = genuine browser, no signer pinning
paths::is_trusted_owner browser branch returns `pinned` where pinned = listed || admin_location (paths.rs:1497-1504)
notes: LIVE EVASION against the 2026-10-25 'pinned' fix. The fix makes an unlisted minor-browser name trusted when EITHER it is in PUBLISHERS (exact signer) OR it sits in an admin-only folder (identity::admin_location: Program Files / WindowsApps / Windows). The admin_location branch applies NO signer check — ANY valid Authenticode signature works. So a binary named thorium.exe (or any of the 47 unpinned BROWSER_IMAGES names), signed with any purchased/stolen OV cert, written to C:\Program Files\Thorium\Application\ is a 'genuine browser': it owns every Chromium and Gecko store, on_dpapi() returns at the genuine_browser guard, and on_net() returns before ST-04/ST-14. Full browser credential theft + DPAPI decrypt + 1.6 MB exfil to a raw IP and api.telegram.org raises only a medium ST-12. Prerequisite: write access to Program Files (admin), e.g. a trojanised/elevated installer (modelled here as a MOTW'd high-integrity setup.exe parent) — a real delivery vector for signed stealer payloads. Root cause: admin_location is treated as a substitute for signer pinning, but a browser *name* in Program Files should still require the real browser's signer. Added by the fix-round red team (2026-10-25); the engine detects it after the red-team fixes.
